bills.title: American Samoa Statutory Nationality and Citizenship Act

To protect collective self-determination and individual rights under Federal statutes conferring nationality on persons born and residing in the territory of American Samoa, to enable subsequent elective United States citizenship upon application of such persons residing in a State or in a territory subject to sections 301 through 308 of the Immigration and Nationality Act, and for other purposes.
South Pacific Tuna Treaty Act of 2025
To amend the Immigration and Nationality Act to waive certain naturalization requirements for United States nationals, and for other purposes.

donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. Employer means where the donor works, not that the company gave money; corporations can't give directly to campaigns. Industry groups use simple keyword rules and may misclassify some donors.

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.

stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.
stands_for.factual_flag: Not yet summarized: this line is built only from the official vote question and the bill's official title.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

A $250,586 CDC award to ASDOH will strengthen epidemiology, laboratory capacity, and infectious disease surveillance in American Samoa.

Thank you to Epidemiologist Adam Konrote, Dr. Saipale Fuimaono, and our medical professionals working to keep our people safe. https://t.co/7M10nwpQYg

It is a delight to celebrate Manu’a Flag Day with our people and Governor Pulaali’i Nikolao Pula. We honor Manu’a’s forefathers, our Toa o Samoa, and the islands of Ta’u, Ofu, and Olosega. May God bless Manu’a!

Pics: 2025 Manu’a Flag Day. https://t.co/uZdcfONO6U

American Samoa has a proud military tradition, with generations of Samoans serving our nation with honor. Staff from Congresswoman Uifa’atali Amata’s office recently participated in Marine Day at Quantico, gaining firsthand insight into Marine Corps readiness and the needs of https://t.co/5iMPO4EnZe

May is AAPI Heritage Month - a time to honor the history, cultures, and contributions of Asian Americans, Native Hawaiians, and Pacific Islanders across the United States.

For American Samoa and Pacific Islanders nationwide, this is a meaningful opportunity to celebrate our https://t.co/GR5nBsrmOr

During National Police Week, I thank our law enforcement officers for their dedication and service to our communities. We rely on their professionalism, readiness, and sacrifice each day. Peace Officers Memorial Day is a poignant reminder of the sacrifice of thousands of officers https://t.co/ZXPzkPi3lz

Illegal fishing hurts our people and our economy.

The FISH Act strengthens enforcement with tougher inspections, penalties, and vessel tracking.

Protecting our waters. Protecting our future. https://t.co/FwHDHfV073

Happy 118th birthday to the U.S. Army Reserve (est. April 23, 1908). Grateful for generations of service, including our Toa o Samoa serving across the Pacific with the 9th MSC.
Your readiness, sacrifice, and commitment keep our nation strong and free. 🇺🇸 https://t.co/T5jueLNeVW

Joined a Veterans town hall at VFW Post 3391 to hear directly from our Veterans and share updates from my work as Vice Chairman of the House Veterans’ Affairs Committee.

We thank our Veterans for their service and leadership. https://t.co/JxR2No6sJs

Blessed Palm Sunday
I send blessings to American Samoa
“Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord, peace in heaven and glory in the highest.” Luke 19:38 https://t.co/MGl4Jvy2yx

I am saddened by the passing of Governor Lolo Letalu Matalasi Moliga. He was a strong and decisive leader, and above all a man of faith. He has a secure place in American Samoa’s history. My deepest condolences to Cynthia Moliga and the entire Moliga family. https://t.co/ZnmH4Rbpp0

From Forbes: During a House Natural Resources Committee hearing in January, Rep. Amata Coleman Radewagen spoke on deep-sea mining and its impact on island communities like American Samoa.

Watch: https://t.co/hz0nkP52pa

This week, I spoke to the House Natural Resources Committee to state American Samoa’s united opposition to seabed mining, submit comments for the record, and question witnesses on environmental risk and technology readiness.
#AmericanSamoa #ProtectOurWaters #HouseNaturalResources https://t.co/V2aK916xQR

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
